newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus still on falling trend--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus still on falling trend--MOF.

text.p: Japan's trade surplus is still basically on a declining trend despite a rise in November, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told a news conference on Wednesday.
"The trade surplus is basically on a declining trend," he told reporters.

Japan's trade surplus in November rose 0.2 percent from a year earlier to 675.19 billion yen, its first rise in two years, the ministry said earlier. The official said MOF saw the rise as steady from the previous month.

He said although the trade balance would be affected by foreign exchange rates, crude oil prices and economic conditions at home and abroad, growth in imports would continue to exceed that of exports.
He attributed the rise in November to an increase in car exports and temporary factors such as a fall in imports of aircraft.
He added that the yen's weakness was one factor in the rise in trade surplus in November. The MOF used an exchange rate of 112.79 yen to the dollar in November, against 101.18 yen a year earlier.
The major reason for the rise in the trade surplus with the United States in November was a 45.7 percent rise in car exports to the U.S., the official said.

The ministry sees car exports to the United States continuing to rise in the coming months. Models such as recreational vehicles which are not produced in the United States had contributed to the rise, the official said.
Another reason for the rise in car exports was the comparison with a relatively low level of car exports a year earlier.
Asked about the outlook for the surplus with the United States, he said it was difficult to make a judgment, as it could be affected by various factors such as the foreign exchange rate.
